analysis: Urea is a waste product formed in the liver from the breakdown of proteins and is excreted in urine. It is not transported to the liver for elimination, but rather produced there. Urea is not degraded to ammonium in the urea cycle; instead, it is the end product of the cycle. Urea is polar due to its ability to form hydrogen bonds, and it does not easily form crystals. It is derived from arginine during the urea cycle, where arginine is converted to urea and ornithine. Urea has two amine groups and one carbonyl group, not two ketone groups and one amino group.
